To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Interposition of reversed jejunal segment (RS) in short bowel (SB), a surgical procedure that has been investigated in human and animal models with promising results, does not influence growth hormone and insulin levels, hormones well known for their role in short bowel pathophysiologic mechanisms.
Interposition of a reversed loop of the small bowel in the pig model does not influence endogenous growth hormone and/or insulin.

endogenous growth hormone and serum insulin did not demonstrate significant difference between the two experimental groups, and therefore did not seem to have direct effect in mechanisms of enhanced intestinal adaption in short bowel syndrome.

the role of endogenous growth hormone and Insulin in the adaptation of the intestine in short bowel syndrome after reversed interposition of a jejunal segment.
the effect of growth hormone and insulin on the adaptation process of the intestine after reversed jejunal loop interposition in short bowel syndrome in a porcine model.
the effect of reversed jejunal segment on the endogenous growth hormone and the insulin in the short bowel syndrome in the porcine model.

growth hormone and insulin are not involved in mechanisms of enhanced intestinal adaption in the reversed group.

the interposition of a reverse jejunal segment is not able to improve growth hormone and insulin levels in a porcine model of short bowel syndrome, and that the effect of reversed jejunal segment interposition on intestinal adaptation is not related to growth hormone and insulin.
